knowledge.text: The beak only takes the banana if its middle is within 7 cm of the beak tip.
Attempts failed even when the banana was 0.09 m away (Step 9), showing distance alone is insufficient for a grab.
If the specific target container (e.g., green box) is not found, searching for a generic type (e.g., box) may lead to the wrong container.
Dropping the banana at 0.28 m distance from the target container does not ensure it is inside the container.
The beak can successfully grab the banana when its middle is 0.05 m from the beak tip.
Walking forward can stop early if an object is near the path.
Searching for the banana or "banana inside green box" repeatedly failed even when close to the target container.
The banana landed at 0.09 m ahead and 0.00 m left, while the green box center was measured at 0.12 m ahead and 0.15 m left.
The calculated drop point does not guarantee the banana lands at the center of the target container.

skills.text: Always verify the banana's orientation relative to the beak tip before attempting to pick it up.
After dropping the banana, verify its location relative to the container to ensure it is fully inside.
When approaching a container, measure the distance and bearing to align the drop point correctly.
When dropping, align the drop point relative to the box dimensions (e.g., 0.20 m across, 0.11 m deep) to ensure it lands inside.
After dropping, measure the banana's location relative to the box to confirm it is fully inside, rather than relying solely on detection.
After dropping, measure both the banana and the container to determine the offset and adjust future drop points accordingly.
